verdict.rationale: Anytype docs strongly claim local-first, fully-offline storage ("All your content is stored locally on your device... the app always works without an internet connection", a device-resident encrypted Vault), which supports the offline half of the story. However, hands-on community reports directly contradict the 'read without the app' requirement: one user notes 'Compared to Obsidian, I can't just use raw Markdown or CSV file with Anytype' and another states 'Seems there is no way to really access or control my files externally,' while a third notes data isn't even encrypted on disk as claimed. This is a concrete, documented contradiction of the plain-local-file ownership claim, not just general skepticism. Missing for 10: evidence of a genuinely human-readable/portable local file format, and independent confirmation that data can be accessed without the Anytype binary.
